subject: Launch sign-off: runtime-1.19 kernel selector v2 (criteria + rollout stages + owners)
related_links: Grafana: runtime-performance / selector_v2 canary dashboard (internal link)
body:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>, Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: 
Date: Sat, Feb 7, 2026 at 11:38 AM -0800
Subject: Launch sign-off: runtime-1.19 kernel selector v2 (criteria + rollout stages + owners)

Mateo / Ava,

We’re queued to cut runtime-1.19 on Tuesday. Before we flip selector v2 beyond internal canary, can we align on:

1) launch criteria (what has to be true before we go from internal -> 5% hosted)
2) rollout stages + minimum bake times
3) who gives the final “go” after the 5% canary results

Current proposed stages (from ENG-3934):
- Stage 0: internal canary (already running)
- Stage 1: Hosted us-east 5% traffic (feature-flagged) + kill switch available
- Stage 2: Hosted us-east 25%
- Stage 3: Hosted all regions 25% (stagger by region)
- Stage 4: Dedicated opt-in (by cluster)
- Stage 5: Default-on for Hosted; keep overrides for Dedicated/Private

Proposed acceptance criteria for Stage 1 -> Stage 2:
- No increase in 5xx rate > +0.05% absolute vs control
- No increase in p95 end-to-end latency > +3% vs control for top 10 routes/models
- No increase in NaN/correctness signals (conformance tests green; no new NaN alerts)
- No sustained GPU OOM/evictions increase (watch KV cache + fragmentation)

If you’re good with the above, I’ll add it to the release train checklist and mark the sign-off owners in the ticket.

Thanks,
Connor

—
Connor O’Brien
Release Engineering
Redwood Inference


From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: 
Date: Sat, Feb 7, 2026 at 12:07 PM -0800
Subject: Re: Launch sign-off: runtime-1.19 kernel selector v2 (criteria + rollout stages + owners)

Thanks Connor.

I’m supportive, with two changes to make this “SRE-signable”:

1) Bake time:
- Stage 1 (5% us-east) should bake for a full peak window. For us that’s 24 hours (not just “a few hours”), unless we’re in a critical situation.

2) Guardrails / rollback criteria should be explicit and binary:
- Any p95 regression > 5% on the canary cohort (vs control) sustained for 30 min = rollback
- Any elevated error rate (5xx) > +0.1% absolute sustained for 10 min = rollback
- Any correctness signal (NaN/inf alert, conformance mismatch) = immediate rollback

Also: please make sure the oncall has a single “kill switch” path, not “it depends which config file you edit.” If there’s a v2 flag + override precedence, we need it documented.

If Mateo is comfortable being the engineering sign-off and Connor runs the mechanics, I can be the reliability sign-off for Stage 1 -> Stage 2.

-Ava

Ava Chen
VP, Engineering
Redwood Inference


From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: 
Date: Sat, Feb 7, 2026 at 12:44 PM -0800
Subject: Re: Launch sign-off: runtime-1.19 kernel selector v2 (criteria + rollout stages + owners)

Agree with Ava’s adjustments.

Let’s lock the sign-off model as:
- Stage 1 enablement (internal -> 5% hosted us-east): Release Eng executes when Runtime says “ready” AND SRE says dashboards/alerts are in place.
- Stage 1 -> Stage 2 (5% -> 25% us-east): requires two explicit approvals:
  (a) Reliability approval: Ava (or SRE delegate if you’re out)
  (b) Runtime approval: me (or Hiro if I’m out)

On criteria:
- Use Ava’s rollback triggers verbatim (binary, sustained windows). Those go in the ENG-3934 checklist and the oncall runbook.
- For the p95 regression number: we can keep Connor’s +3% as the “don’t proceed” threshold, but rollback at +5% sustained is fine.

On kill switch:
- Please ensure the kill switch is: selector_v2_enabled=false at the top level (no per-model exceptions needed to disable).
- Overrides can exist, but we should not require overrides to roll back.

Connor: can you update the release checklist and reply here with the exact dashboard links + where the kill switch lives?

Thanks,
Mateo

—
Mateo Alvarez
VP Engineering, Runtime
Redwood Inference


From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>, Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: 
Date: Sat, Feb 7, 2026 at 1:23 PM -0800
Subject: Re: Launch sign-off: runtime-1.19 kernel selector v2 (criteria + rollout stages + owners)

Done.

Updates:
- ENG-3934 checklist updated with:
  - 24h bake requirement at Stage 1
  - rollback triggers (p95 +5%/30m, 5xx +0.1%/10m, any NaN/inf) + “one-click” rollback step
  - sign-off owners: Ava (reliability) + Mateo (runtime) for Stage 1 -> 2

Kill switch path (documented + verified by Benji):
- runtime config: selector_v2_enabled: false (global)
- precedence: global disable overrides all per-model-family entries

Dashboards:
- Runtime perf: selector v2 canary compare (control vs v2): (internal grafana link)
- Errors: 5xx + timeouts by selector_version: (internal grafana link)
- Correctness: NaN/inf + conformance signal: (internal grafana link)

Next step: I’ll schedule the Stage 1 enablement for Tue 10am PT pending “ready” from Runtime.

Connor


From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: 
Date: Sat, Feb 7, 2026 at 2:12 PM -0800
Subject: Re: Launch sign-off: runtime-1.19 kernel selector v2 (criteria + rollout stages + owners)

Approved on my side given the above, with the assumption the oncall runbook references the same single kill switch.

If anything trips the rollback criteria, default action is rollback first, investigate second.

-Ava
